Chapter 6: Embedding Change Through Daily Practice and Triggers
So, you’ve made the commitment to change. What comes next? Well, it’s about weaving those new behaviors into your everyday life—making them feel as natural as your morning coffee. Change isn’t just a single moment. It’s really a collection of small, repeated choices you make day in and day out.
Here’s the tricky part: old habits love to sneak back in, especially when you’re faced with stress, a tight deadline, or maybe even that one colleague who always seems to push your buttons. That’s why recognizing your triggers is so important. It’s the difference between running on autopilot and making a conscious choice.
Imagine triggers as that starting gun at the beginning of a race. They set off a chain reaction—cue, routine, reward. Now, this can either pull you back into an old habit or open up a space for something new. The real magic happens when you notice these moments and use them to make a different, more intentional move.
So, how do you actually do this? Here’s a simple approach:
First, pay attention to the situations or emotions that tend to spark those unhelpful behaviors. Next, when a trigger pops up, pause for just a moment. Give yourself that little window to choose how you’ll respond. Then, swap out the old reaction for something more constructive. And after it’s over? Take a minute to reflect—what worked, and what could you tweak next time?
Let’s say you’re in a heated discussion, and you notice the urge to interrupt. Instead, you take a slow, deliberate breath and really listen before jumping in. At first, this pause might feel awkward, but with practice, it starts to become second nature. Eventually, it replaces that old reflex.
Daily practice is absolutely key. Think about it like an athlete training their muscles—the more you repeat a new behavior, the stronger it gets. Maybe you set a daily intention, like “Today, I’ll focus on giving credit to others,” and at the end of the day, you check in with yourself to see how it went.
Visual reminders can be super helpful too. Try a sticky note on your monitor or a little calendar alert that pops up right when you need it most. Those gentle nudges keep your commitment front and center, especially when you’re busy or under pressure.
Remember, this isn’t about being perfect—it’s about making progress. Every day gives you a fresh shot to practice, reflect, and make small adjustments. Over time, those little acts add up to something truly meaningful and lasting.
